blocks.text: Sapperton Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Sapperton is the slope neighbourhood above the Fraser River between McBride Boulevard and Brunette Creek, taking in Royal Columbian Hospital, the Sapperton and Braid SkyTrain stations, Hume Park and the Brewery District.
The name comes from the Royal Engineers' Columbia Detachment camp: "Sappers' Town," from 1858, is the origin of the Sapperton name.
East Columbia Street is the spine, carrying the 109 bus between New Westminster Station and Lougheed Station.

blocks.text: Sapperton Houses: the housing stock

items.t: 6680, 2001, with the RT-A and RT-B townhouse districts applying where the Official Community Plan designates them.
The station areas at Sapperton and Braid are a Frequent Transit Development Area, so the slope's house streets sit beside a designated growth area rather than inside a static enclave.

blocks.text: Sapperton Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Flood rules bite at the bottom of the slope, not on it: the Brunette River industrial land is Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level, while the residential slope above is not the risk pocket.

blocks.text: Sapperton Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Hume Park and Lower Hume Park, by the Brunette River, hold the pool, lacrosse box and off-leash area, and the Brunette-Fraser Greenway and Sapperton Landing Park tie the slope to the Fraser waterfront.
Sapperton Park dates to 1907, making it one of the city's oldest park sites.
The Brewery District is the former Labatt brewery site on East Columbia Street, redeveloped by Wesgroup as 1.4 million square feet across 8 buildings, 7 of them complete.

blocks.text: Sapperton Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Brewery District, East Columbia Street, Wesgroup, redevelopment of the former Labatt brewery site: 1.4 million square feet across 8 buildings with 7 complete, including Building 1 at 290 East Columbia Street (2013), the TransLink and Transit Police headquarters office over retail, and Building 2 at 200 East Columbia Street (2010) — STATUS: 7 of 8 buildings complete, read 2026-11-03.

Royal Columbian Hospital redevelopment, 330 East Columbia Street, Fraser Health: the Jim Pattison Acute Care Tower opened to patients May 31, 2026, and Phases 2 and 3 total about 2 billion dollars — STATUS: tower open; later phases in delivery, read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Sapperton Houses: getting around

items.t: Sapperton and Braid stations, both on the Expo Line, serve the area's two ends, and the 109 bus runs on East Columbia Street between New Westminster Station and Lougheed Station.
McBride Boulevard is the west-side route off the slope, and Brunette Creek and the Brunette-Fraser Greenway frame the east side.

blocks.text: Sapperton Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check flood position by elevation: the Brunette River industrial land at the slope's foot is Floodplain Zone 4 below the Flood Construction Level, so a low-lying lot needs a flood check even though the residential slope is not the risk pocket.
Expect hospital-area construction and traffic through the later redevelopment phases at Royal Columbian Hospital.
Confirm the SD40 catchment for the exact address, since the recorded chain for 331 Richmond Street does not settle other Sapperton streets.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Sapperton?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 13 houses listed in Sapperton. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Sapperton a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Sapperton had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Sapperton from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 6 houses sold in Sapperton over those 5 months, out of 75 in all of New Westminster.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Sapperton?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: What is the new elementary school's story?
faq.a: Skwo:wech Elementary opened June 6, 2022 at a cost of 34.98 million dollars for more than 400 Kindergarten to Grade 5 students, replacing Richard McBride Elementary, and its name is the halq'eméylem word for sturgeon.

faq.q: What changed at Royal Columbian Hospital?
faq.a: Royal Columbian Hospital, at 330 East Columbia Street, is Fraser Health's regional referral hospital for cardiology, neurosurgery, high-risk obstetrics and neonatal intensive care, and its Jim Pattison Acute Care Tower opened to patients May 31, 2026 — 10 storeys, 388 beds, with a new emergency department and entrance.

faq.q: What did houses in Sapperton sell for?
faq.a: 14 houses sold in Sapperton between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,420,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Sapperton?
faq.a: The median was 26 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.4% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
